- 2026-09-01 [claude] Third bug in the same chain: after the --machine fix, lege-resourced restarted fine but the activation gate still reported "came back without writing a build stamp". Root cause: RealStamps::read() (cli/lege/src/dev/systemd.rs) called lege_build::read_stamps(), which resolves its directory from the CURRENT process's own $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -- root's (unset under sudo), not the desktop user's /run/user/<uid>/legeos/build where user-scope units (everything except hostd/boot-health) actually write. Fixed by having RealStamps merge /run/legeos/build (system scope) with the target user's resolved /run/user/<uid>/legeos/build (user scope, uid read from /etc/passwd via SUDO_USER) when running as root.  `@legeos.papercut.third-bug-in-the-same-chain-after-the-machine/1`

Root cause: RealSystemctl/RealBusProbe in cli/lege/src/dev/systemd.rs ran `systemctl --user`/`busctl --user` as root, which has no session bus of its own -- a --user unit lives in the desktop user's manager. - 2026-09-01 [claude] `lege dev deploy` restarts lege-hostd.service and it crash-loops: zbus fails "claiming org.legeos.Host on the system bus" with a raw EACCES connecting to /var/run/dbus/system_bus_socket (0666, root:root). Ruled out: AppArmor profile is confirmed complain-mode (would only log, not block); org.legeos.Host.conf is correctly shipped under /usr/share/dbus-1/system.d/; a plain `sudo -u root` shell can read/write the socket fine. - 2026-09-01 [claude] `lege dev deploy` failed with apt "unauthenticated packages" right after a fresh `lege dev repo init --install-source` on a machine with a stale cached index. Root cause: every publish regenerates the devrepo Release from scratch, so apt sometimes sees an Origin/Label mismatch vs. its cached copy and silently keeps the stale (mismatched) index instead of refreshing — unlike scripts/reinstall-legeos-desktop.sh, which uses dpkg -i directly and never touches apt's trust cache. Fixed by adding --allow-releaseinfo-change to the scoped apt-get update in refresh_index() (cli/lege/src/dev/install.rs); this repo has exactly one publisher so accepting the metadata change is always correct.  `@legeos.papercut.lege-dev-deploy-failed-with-apt-unauthenticated/1`
- 2026-09-01 [claude] lege-build's tests created a scratch directory under /tmp and removed it at the start of the NEXT run — one run behind — so 287 stale directories had accumulated on the dev machine before anyone noticed. Fixed by moving to tempfile (a full cargo test --workspace now leaves nothing behind, verified by counting), but the pattern is worth watching for in other test code.  `@legeos.papercut.lege-build-s-tests-created-a-scratch-directory/1`
- 2026-09-01 [claude] First user run of the deploy path failed at cargo deb -p lege: the components.toml asset was workspace-root-relative but cargo-deb resolves static assets against the crate dir, and no CI stage runs cargo-deb, so 'just check' was green throughout. Fixed the path and added an asset-source existence check to check-packaging; also 'cargo xtask' was documented but the alias never existed (.cargo/config.toml now defines it).  `@legeos.papercut.first-user-run-of-the-deploy-path-failed-at/1`
- 2026-09-01 [claude] Correcting my earlier papercut: --allow-releaseinfo-change was not the fix (the scoped apt-get update always succeeded cleanly). Real cause: source_stanza() in cli/lege/src/dev/repo.rs wrote `Trusted: no`, which forces every package unauthenticated unconditionally in apt's deb822 semantics -- it does NOT mean "trust only if Signed-By verifies".
